text.p: Cullen/Frost Bankers Inc chairman Tom Frost said Monday the firm was not interested in merging with a larger bank and was instead intent on expanding through acquisitions and internal growth.

Frost told Reuters in an interview that the $5 billion bank, which operates in South Texas from its San Antonio base, was considering the purchase of a money management firm, while at the same time keeping an eye out for smaller banks to buy.
"That's not in our plans," Frost said when asked if the bank had had any buyout offers.

"They (acquiring banks) seem to be looking at banks of $10 billion and up. I don't see any activity on banks of our size around the country. But that's neither here nor there...we're not in the dance."

Cullen/Frost has long been rumored to be a buyout candidate because of its strong financial performance. It was the only one of Texas' 10 biggest banks to survive the oil bust of the 1980s and now is on a solid financial footing.

The company earned $1.33 a share in the first half of the year, up from $1.16 for the same period in 1996. Analysts have forecast earnings of $2.68 a share for all of 1997, compared with $2.40 the year before.
Frost agreed earnings growth would continue.
"We'll continue to have reasonable progress. I'm not looking forward to flat earnings," he said.

Cullen/Frost has acquired nine banks, with total assets of $1.3 billion, since 1993. Frost said it would consider other purchases in areas where it already operates, "but we're not actively pursuing anybody there."
After so many buys in the past few years, "there's sort of been a lull, which is good for us because we've been able to ingest what we've got," he said.
The purchase of a money management firm was possible.
"We have started saying we ought to think about people in the investment business...a money manager, not necessarily a broker, because that fits more what we do," he said.
The bank was about a third of the way through a 500,000 share stock buyback authorized by the board in 1996.
"We hope we'll get that done before the year-end and then we can consider whether we want another one or not," he said.
A strong regional economy portended well for the bank's performance.
"The economy looks good where we are and we expect to just continue to ride along with that," he added.
